Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Despite Modi's popularity, why is the BJP losing elections?
Answer: Modi’s popularity is on an average getting around 15% to 20% votes in every state for the party. To win an election the BJP require around 40%+ of votes. The balance of 20%+ votes the party gets because of the party, the candidates and other issues of the election. Hence Modi’s popularity alone do not win any election for the people. Also other aspects of the election too alone do not win election for the party. Apart from these aspects the popularity of regional parties or regional leaders too count in the victory of BJP. If their popularity exceeds that of BJP and Modi, naturally these regional parties win in those states. In WB, Tamilnadu, Kerala, Punjab, and few more states the regional parties and Congress have done well to win majority of the seats. Sometimes issues take precedence over other aspects such as popularity of Modi or other regional leaders. In 2024 the Khata Khat has taken precedence over every other popular aspects of the election. Not less than 15% of voters are swayed by the same. Hence Modi’s popularity alone is never decisive for any election for victory or defeat.

Question: Is there a possibility of an anti-Kejriwal sentiment during the upcoming assembly election in Delhi?
Answer: We don’t know whether there is anti-Kejriwal sentiment is present during the coming assembly election. But aspersions have spread because of his involvement in the Delhi Excise Policy scam. Kejriwal may not get the same reception he has been getting in 2015 and 2020. The trust that the people had earlier may not continue. The Lok Sabha election states that Kejriwal is still popular because AAP got more votes in 2024 than 2019. This may be attributed because of the alliance with Congress. How it pans out needs to be watched. If Kejriwal is not available for campaigning, AAP to give a good result will never happen. If the case against Kejriwal in Delhi Excise Policy scam comes to an end with his conviction, AAP will see its worst result. If he comes out unscathed, probability of Kejriwal producing another stunning victory is on the cards. Everything depends on Court verdict.

Question: Who is going to form a government in Delhi if the elections are going to be right now, AAP, Congress, or BJP?

This does not mean that BJP will form the government nor Congress wins. The hung situation is probable. May be the Congress and AAP form a coalition government. Even if BJP adds 4% to 6%, can just sweep the state. Also AAP will poll less than 40% to lose the election. Freebie will not come to the help of AAP because Congress and BJP will not fall behind in this aspect and offer more freebies.
